question: Suppose $f(x) = \begin{cases} x^2, & x \geq 0 \\ 2x-1, & x < 0\end{cases}$. Is $f(x)$ differentiable at $x=0$?
explanation:
Check continuity at $x=0$:

$\lim_{x \to 0^-} f(x) = -1$

$\lim_{x \to 0^+} f(x) = 0$

Since left and right limits are not equal, function is not continuous.

Therefore, it is not differentiable at $x=0$.

options.B: No, $f(x)$ is not differentiable at $x=0$ because it is not continuous there
options.D: No, $f(x)$ is continuous but not differentiable at $x=0$
